No long-term randomized studies of alcohol and ischaemic heart disease exist; short-term studies show dose-dependent effects on surrogate markers (higher HDL cholesterol, less platelet activation, lower fibrinogen, anti-inflammatory effects), and HDL cholesterol is also raised by regular heavy drinking and is highest in people with alcohol use disorder. The authors judge the ADH1B Mendelian randomization study (Holmes et al., 2014), which concluded there was no protective effect, difficult to compare with the epidemiology because the variant was also linked to less binge drinking, while adding that Mendelian randomization studies may become a very useful tool.
